root_cause.text: During conversion to dynamic IDs, two link entries in the SM8450 interconnect driver were left as legacy symbolic node IDs instead of direct pointers to node structures, causing a NULL pointer dereference when the interconnect framework dereferences the destination link.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `.link_nodes = { MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG }` to `.link_nodes = { &qhm_nsp_noc_config }` and `.link_nodes = { MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC }` to `.link_nodes = { &qhm_config_noc }`. The commit message states "left two links unconverted" and the call trace points to `icc_link_nodes+0x3c/0x100`.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
interconnect: qcom: sm8450: convert to dynamic IDs

Stop using fixed and IDs and covert the platform to use dynamic IDs
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 51513bec806fbe1cf9254baed97f115a480bbb53
Author: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 31 16:45:37 2025 +0200

    interconnect: qcom: sm8450: convert to dynamic IDs
    
    Stop using fixed and IDs and covert the platform to use dynamic IDs for
    the interconnect. This gives more flexibility and also allows us to drop
    the .num_links member, saving from possible errors related to it being
    not set or set incorrectly.
    
    Signed-off-by: Dmitry
bic_trace_step.reason: Two nodes, qhs_compute_cfg and qhs_lpass_cfg, have their .link_nodes set to legacy symbolic IDs (MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG and MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC) instead of direct pointers to node structures. This matches the root cause description of left-behind legacy IDs causing NULL pointer dereference. All other nodes are properly converted with &node_name pointers.

    platforms. The topology consists of several NoCs that are controlled by
